title: The Sum of Our Technology
summary: What if AI acceleration fails outside a code generator? Two shifts in software engineering demand evidence, sustainable delivery and viable socio-technical control.

rights.notice: Article by Vitalii Oborskyi, existing AI-generated cover, seven exact full-page PMDay v35 source screenshots. Original deck/source/third-party credits retained; per-item publication clearance pending.

assets.alt: Conceptual architecture connects software construction with a branching decision structure.
assets.caption: We can delegate more work. We still have to own the consequences.
assets.credit: AI-generated editorial illustration directed for this article; built-in ImageGen, 15 October 2026.

assets.alt: First slide of the PMDay presentation, AI Changes the Delivery System and the Product Itself.
assets.caption: PMDay presentation, v35 review edition, 15 slides. Recording in Ukrainian.
assets.credit: Vitalii Oborskyi. Preview rendered from the pinned v35 PDF; presentation credits remain in the source deck.

assets.alt: PMDay slide 3: code-generation capacity increases to 100 changes a week, but review and integration remain at eight; 92 uncompleted changes accumulate in the illustrative push system.
assets.caption: Accelerating code generation is not the same as accelerating delivery. Illustrative fixed-capacity scenario; PMDay v35, slide 3.
assets.credit: Full-page screenshot of PMDay 2026 v35 review slide 3 by Vitalii Oborskyi. Source-deck and third-party credits preserved; publication rights pending.

assets.alt: PMDay slide 5: illustrative generation output grows faster than team comprehension, showing a possible—not measured—comprehension gap.
assets.caption: The potential comprehension gap is a scenario, not a measured cognitive ceiling. PMDay v35, slide 5.
assets.credit: Full-page screenshot of PMDay 2026 v35 review slide 5 by Vitalii Oborskyi. Source-deck and third-party credits preserved; publication rights pending.

assets.alt: PMDay slide 7: teams measure flow, maintainability, production and recovery while experimenting with candidate controls to find a sustainable AI-assisted SDLC equilibrium.
assets.caption: Search for a sustainable workflow, not a return to the old one: measure outcomes and test countermeasures. Proposed measures are not proven fixes. PMDay v35, slide 7.
assets.credit: Full-page screenshot of PMDay 2026 v35 review slide 7 by Vitalii Oborskyi. Source-deck and third-party credits preserved; publication rights pending.

assets.alt: PMDay slide 9: traditional exact-path requirements contrast with a space of acceptable responses—answer, clarify or escalate—bounded by context, permissions and forbidden disclosure.
assets.caption: Model-dependent behaviour demands precise boundaries, examples, prohibitions and coverage across contexts—not a single canonical wording. PMDay v35, slide 9.
assets.credit: Full-page screenshot of PMDay 2026 v35 review slide 9 by Vitalii Oborskyi. Source-deck and third-party credits preserved; publication rights pending.

assets.alt: PMDay slide 10: in 200 synthetic responses, 196 are acceptable, three instructions are incorrect and one disclosure violates a release prohibition despite a 98% acceptable average.
assets.caption: The average cannot cancel a forbidden consequence. Synthetic evaluation, sample uncertainty and a specific release-blocking rule. PMDay v35, slide 10.
assets.credit: Full-page screenshot of PMDay 2026 v35 review slide 10 by Vitalii Oborskyi. Source-deck and third-party credits preserved; publication rights pending.

assets.alt: PMDay slide 12: a model proposal is checked before consequential action; failed checks take a denial or fallback route, while monitoring and authorised intervention support ongoing control.
assets.caption: Effective control spans permission enforcement, safe fallback and verified intervention, not observation alone. PMDay v35, slide 12.
assets.credit: Full-page screenshot of PMDay 2026 v35 review slide 12 by Vitalii Oborskyi. Source-deck and third-party credits preserved; publication rights pending.

assets.alt: PMDay slide 14: normal delivery obligations continue alongside a bounded experiment and reassessment loop fed by production outcomes, incidents and authorised release decisions.
assets.caption: Keep delivery commitments while the learning loop remains open after release. Production outcomes can change future evidence, control and authority decisions. PMDay v35, slide 14.
assets.credit: Full-page screenshot of PMDay 2026 v35 review slide 14 by Vitalii Oborskyi. Source-deck and third-party credits preserved; publication rights pending.
